issues.legal_issue: A written arbitration clause may operate as an independent agreement and remain enforceable even when the underlying memorandum does not become a finalized substantive contract.
material_facts: The parties signed a memorandum recording a proposed joint venture and setting out commercial terms, but the contemplated project did not proceed to a finalized agreement.

The memorandum included a written clause requiring unresolved disputes concerning the memorandum, its implementation, breach, termination, or interpretation to be referred to a sole arbitrator after an attempt at amicable resolution.
The respondent later cancelled the memorandum, alleging that the appellant had failed to comply with its terms, and the parties disagreed about their respective obligations.
The appellant sought an amicable resolution, then proposed an arbitrator; the respondent refused to agree to a reference, after which the appellant applied for appointment of an arbitrator.
issues.conclusion: The arbitration clause was a valid, independent arbitration agreement notwithstanding the failure to finalize the proposed substantive agreement. Because amicable resolution failed and the parties did not appoint an arbitrator under their agreed procedure, the Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court’s decision, and appointed a sole arbitrator.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16(1)(a) and (b) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitration clause forming part of a contract is treated as an agreement independent of the other terms, and a finding that the underlying contract is null and void does not automatically invalidate the clause. The separability principle also applies where the underlying transaction is alleged to be unconcluded. The Court relied on Reva Electric Car Company Private Ltd. v. Green Mobil, Today Homes and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. Ludhiana Improvement Trust, and Enercon (India) Limited v. Enercon GMBH. It considered SBP & Co. v. Patel Engineering Ltd. and National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Boghara Polyfab Pvt. Ltd. but found no contrary principle, and held that Section 11 permitted appointment after the agreed procedure failed.

predicates.arbitrator_appointment_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding seeking appointment of an arbitrator after the other party did not agree to the proposed appointment.
predicates.written_transaction_contains_arbitration: The parties recorded an agreement to arbitrate in writing as part of a transaction between them.
predicates.clause_covers_disputes_about_transaction: The written clause covers disputes arising from the transaction, including disputes about its implementation, breach, termination, or interpretation.
predicates.parties_failed_to_resolve_dispute_amicab: The parties attempted or had the opportunity to pursue the agreed amicable resolution process but did not settle the dispute.
predicates.parties_failed_to_appoint_arbitrator_by_: The parties did not appoint an arbitrator in accordance with their agreed appointment procedure.

issues.definition: When an appointment proceeding concerns a written transaction containing a broad arbitration clause, and the parties neither resolve the dispute amicably nor appoint an arbitrator by their agreed procedure, the rule provides for the court to appoint a sole arbitrator.
